claims.content: To maintain records of service providers who treat voucher clients and submit claims for reimbursement via the VMU system.

goal.raw_text: To maintain records of service providers who treat voucher clients and submit claims for reimbursement via the VMU system.

claims.content: VMU User
The VMU User must be logged into the system with appropriate user privileges to access service provider maintenance functions.
The system must have existing User Groups and Individual Users configured, as only the system admin can create User Groups and individual users under them.
The system must be running on the Oracle 9i platform with VB front end and Crystal Reports 9 for reporting capabilities.
High intrusion controls and access level controls must be in place in the system and database, including granular model settings for organizational level user access.
A VMU User initiates the process to add, edit, or delete service provider records in the system.

trigger.raw_text: A VMU User initiates the process to add, edit, or delete service provider records in the system.

claims.content: The VMU User accesses the service provider maintenance screen within the system.
The system displays options for New (adding new records), Edit (updating available records), and Delete (deleting records if no child records are created).
If adding a new service provider, the VMU User enters mandatory information including Group Name (selected from existing User Groups), User Name, Password, and Verify Password.
The system validates that the Password and Verify Password values are equal before saving the user information.
The system checks that the User Name does not already exist to prevent duplicate names.
The system saves the service provider record only if all validation checks pass.
If editing an existing service provider, the VMU User selects the record and updates allowable fields; the system enforces access level controls based on the user’s privileges.
If deleting a service provider, the system verifies that no child records (e.g., claims or transactions) have been created for that provider before allowing deletion.
The system logs the action and updates the database with sequential links and surrogate keys to maintain storage efficiency.
If the Password and Verify Password values are not equal, the system shall not save the user information and shall prompt the VMU User to re-enter matching passwords.
If the VMU User attempts to create a User Group or Individual User with an existing name, the system shall reject the creation and notify the user of the duplicate name error.

If the VMU User attempts to delete a service provider record that has associated child records (e.g., claims or transactions), the system shall prevent deletion and display an error indicating dependent records exist.

If the VMU User lacks appropriate access level privileges for editing or deleting a specific service provider record, the system shall deny the action based on granular model settings and organizational level user controls.
The service provider record is successfully added, updated, or deleted in the database with sequential links and surrogate keys to ensure storage efficiency.
If a new service provider was created, their user information (Group Name, User Name, Password) is stored only after password verification and uniqueness checks.
Access level controls and granular model settings are enforced for all modifications, ensuring only authorized VMU Users can perform specific actions on service provider records.
No duplicate User Names or User Groups exist in the system after successful completion of the use case.
Deletion of a service provider record is permitted only if no child records (e.g., claims or transactions) have been created for that provider.
